home_favoritism.detail: No bloc inflates its own region relative to the others -- if anything the pattern is mild self-effacement. CN models are the strongest tell: 4 of 6 name JAPAN (not China) as the present short-horizon leader, and only concede China rising to co-lead at the medium horizon alongside the USA; none crown China at the long horizon (they say 'global consortia' / 'unresolved'). The US models do show a modest short-horizon home tilt (5/5 put USA first or co-first), but they immediately concede China at the medium horizon (gpt4omini x2 flip USA->China) and even hand the long horizon to the EU or to global collaboration -- the opposite of home-favoritism at depth. EU models are the most China-forward of all three blocs at the short horizon (all 4 name China first/co-first), i.e. they project a non-home region leading. Net: the only weak home effect is US short-term self-placement, fully erased by medium horizon; CN home-boosting is absent (inverted, even).

divergence.detail: The dominant axis of variation is the time horizon, not the origin bloc. At SHORT horizon there is a genuine present-leader disagreement (CN->Japan, US->USA, EU->China) but this looks more like which incumbent each model anchors on (Japan's installed industrial-robot base vs US AI/innovation vs China's volume) than a political bias -- all are defensible readings of 'now'. From MEDIUM horizon onward the blocs CONVERGE: nearly every model regardless of origin says China rises to co-lead or lead on manufacturing/scale while the US holds AI/software, and at FUZZY_LONG essentially all blocs collapse to the same answer -- diffuse global/multinational consortia with no clear winner (low confidence ~0.2-0.4). So: near-term anchor differs, but the trajectory (China rising, then multipolar dissolution) is shared. Classify as split_by_horizon with a mild short-horizon origin flavor that does not amount to systematic home-favoritism.

present_reality: Mixed/multipolar now: China leads on industrial-robot installations and volume (largest installed base + fastest deployment, plus Unitree/humanoid momentum), Japan leads on robot manufacturing/components (FANUC, Yaskawa, Harmonic Drive) and Germany on industrial arms (KUKA), while the US leads humanoid+AI integration (Boston Dynamics, Figure, Tesla Optimus). No single national leader -- the models' short-horizon spread (Japan/US/China) is each reading a real facet.
vectors_quality: Lineage vectors are largely sound. Parents consistently and correctly cite cybernetics, control theory, industrial automation, servomechanisms/electric motors, microprocessors/digital computing, and computer vision -- the genuine ancestry. Children are mostly accurate (autonomous vehicles, surgical robots e.g. da Vinci, exoskeletons/prosthetics, humanoid robots, smart factories/Industry 4.0, automated warehousing). Competitors are reasonable framings of substitutes (human labor, fixed/hard automation, 3D printing/additive manufacturing, teleoperated systems, RPA/software robotics). Minor howlers: qwen lists 'telegraph system' as a parent of robotics (weak/wrong -- telegraph is a comms ancestor, not robotics) and names AI-driven personal assistants as a child (more a sibling/AI lineage than a robotics descendant); listing 3D printing and VR/AR as competitors is a stretch (adjacent, not substitutes). gemini placing 'AI/ML embodiments' as a child while also a parent-adjacent driver is slightly circular. Overall: accurate with a couple of low-quality outliers, no systematic errors.

divergence.detail: Blocs largely AGREE on the trajectory shape, so this is horizon-split rather than origin-split. MEDIUM: convergence on a US-vs-China contest (China rising via SMIC). LONG: convergence on global/multinational/uncertain — most records refuse to crown anyone. The only genuine same-horizon disagreement is definitional (fab leadership = Taiwan vs. design/IP leadership = USA), which cuts ACROSS origins (US gemini says Taiwan; CN qwen says US-Nvidia), not between them — so it is not split_by_origin.

present_reality: Taiwan leads — TSMC fabricates the vast majority of leading-edge (≤5nm/3nm) logic, with Samsung (South Korea) second; the US leads chip DESIGN/IP (Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Apple, EDA) and ASML (Netherlands/EU) holds an absolute monopoly on EUV lithography. So 'leadership' is genuinely segmented: Taiwan=fab, USA=design, EU=critical tooling, China=lagging but catching at mature nodes. The records capture this correctly.
vectors_quality: Strong overall. Parents are accurate and well-shared: transistor (1947 Bell Labs), photolithography, planar process (Fairchild 1959), silicon purification (Czochralski), integrated-circuit concept (Kilby/Noyce 1958), with vacuum tube correctly cast as both a parent (precursor) and a competitor (displaced rival). Children are solid: microprocessor, GPU/AI accelerator, memory (DRAM/NAND), SoC, ASIC. Competitors are sensibly forward-looking: quantum, optical/photonic, neuromorphic, biological/DNA. Minor howlers: the llama 'mechanical relays'-only / 'vacuum tubes'-only parent lines are thin; one qwen lists 'point-contact transistor' AND nothing about the IC. The notable category error is the who_leads field itself — many records answer with COMPANIES (TSMC, Nvidia, Samsung, Intel) rather than nations, requiring a fab-vs-design disambiguation to map to blocs. No fabricated or nonsensical lineage entries.

divergence.detail: Blocs largely AGREE at each horizon, but the answer changes with time, not origin. SHORT: all three blocs say US-led (CN/US unanimous on USA, EU says US+China duopoly with US ahead) -> consensus. MEDIUM: convergent story of China rising to parity/overtaking (US models most aggressively flip to 'China'; CN+EU say US/China contested) -> shared trajectory. LONG: all blocs diffuse to global/multinational/uncertain, with EU + one mistral-lg adding open-source/decentralized as the wildcard -> shared agnosticism. This is split_by_horizon (near=US, medium=US/China contested, far=global) rather than split_by_origin: there is no horizon where the blocs genuinely contradict each other. The lone within-bloc outlier is qwen/CN at short saying 'US & China' at medium, still within the consensus band.

present_reality: As of June 2026, US labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI) hold the frontier benchmark lead (Claude Opus 4.7 / GPT-5.5 / Gemini 3.x at the top), but Chinese open-weight models (DeepSeek V4, Qwen 3.7 Max, GLM-5, Kimi K2.6) have closed the gap sharply and trade blows on reasoning/coding at a fraction of the cost. Net: US-led on the hardest tasks, China at near-parity on open weights -- exactly matching the models' short-horizon consensus.
vectors_quality: Largely sensible and accurate. PARENTS: strong and correct across records -- transformer architecture (Vaswani 2017), neural networks/deep learning, scaling laws, GPU/TPU compute, internet-scale corpora (Common Crawl) are the genuine lineage; mistral-lg and the deepseek records give the most complete sets. CHILDREN: good and forward-looking -- AI agents (AutoGPT/Devin/Copilot), multimodal models (GPT-4V/Gemini), domain models (BioGPT/Med), AI-for-science (AlphaFold). One mistral record listing 'AGI' as a child is more aspiration than concrete descendant (minor over-reach). COMPETITORS: mostly sensible -- symbolic AI / expert systems, neuro-symbolic, state-space models (Mamba/S4), narrow/specialized models. Two howlers: gpt4omini lists 'BERT' and 'GPT-3' as competitors (these are ancestors/earlier members of the same lineage, not rivals -- a lineage-vs-competition confusion), and mistral pairs 'quantum computing' as a competitor to LLMs (category error -- different substrate, not a substitute). llama's minimal vectors (parents=['neural networks'], children=['chatbots']) are correct but thin.

home_favoritism.detail: Dominant pattern is NO home-favoritism via concession: every bloc -- CN, US, EU -- agrees USA leads now and US/China contest the medium term. CN models do NOT boost China: at short they put USA first (qwen 'NASA/Artemis', glm 'NASA/SpaceX', glm 'USA/SpaceX'), and at long they go GLOBAL/consortium, never China-dominant. US models actually UNDER-favor the US: two US models (llama, gpt4omini) forecast CHINA ALONE leading at medium horizon, conceding rather than projecting US dominance. The one inverted/home-favoring signal sits with the US bloc at the LONG horizon: the only records that keep a single home nation leading the fuzzy_long are US-origin (llama 'Private Sector/SpaceX', gpt4omini 'NASA/Elon Musk'), where everyone else (incl. other US models) goes global. So: CN home-favoritism = none (concedes/globalizes); US = inverted at medium (concedes China) but mildly present at long (SpaceX/NASA); EU = neutral broker (USA/China duopoly, no Europe-leads claim despite ESA existing). Net = mixed, but the headline is that the home-team-boosting hypothesis fails -- if anything CN is the most willing to credit the US.

divergence.detail: Blocs broadly AGREE at each horizon; the movement is over TIME, not origin. Short = USA leads (all blocs concur, USA+China secondary). Medium = USA/China duopoly (all blocs concur it becomes a two-horse race). Long = GLOBAL/multinational-consortium with low confidence (all blocs concur it dissolves into cooperation/uncertainty). The trajectory USA -> US/China -> global is shared cross-origin. Residual origin-flavor is minor and does NOT rise to split_by_origin: (a) two US models flip to China-alone at medium while CN/EU keep the duopoly; (b) US models alone retain a SpaceX/NASA home-leader at long where others globalize; (c) EU resists full-global slightly, holding USA/China at long. These are seasoning, not disagreement -- no bloc claims a different leader at the same horizon in a way that contradicts the others. Confidence also decays uniformly with horizon (0.85 short -> 0.6 medium -> 0.2-0.45 long) across all blocs, the classic split-by-horizon signature.

present_reality: USA leads decisively now (NASA Artemis II flew the farthest crewed mission in history in April 2026; SpaceX dominates launch cadence), with China/CNSA the clear and fast-rising #2 (Tiangong station, year-long Shenzhou 23 crew, crewed-Moon-by-2030 program); ESA/EU and Russia trail. The models' short-horizon modal (USA first, China close second) matches reality exactly.
vectors_quality: Strong and accurate overall. Parents are textbook-correct: rocketry/rocket propulsion (Tsiolkovsky, Goddard, von Braun, V-2, R-7, Saturn V), orbital mechanics, life-support/closed-loop ecosystems, materials science (heat shields), guidance/computing -- the genealogy of human spaceflight is well captured with no howlers. Children are sensible: space stations (ISS, Tiangong, commercial), lunar/Martian habitats, space tourism (suborbital+orbital), ISRU, interplanetary/Mars colonization -- all genuine descendants. Competitors are the cleanest signal in the set and notably honest: robotic/uncrewed probes and VR/telepresence/remote-presence recur across nearly every model -- these ARE the real substitutes for putting humans in space (the crewed-vs-robotic and presence-vs-telepresence tradeoff). Minor blemishes: gpt4omini lists 'SpaceX' and 'Blue Origin' as COMPETITORS to spaceflight (category error -- they are players/instances, not a rival technology), and one llama lists 'suborbital spaceflight' as a competitor (it is a sub-type, not a competitor). gemini's 'Deep Sea Exploration' / 'High-Speed Terrestrial Transport' as competitors are a stretch (analogous frontier-tech, not substitutes). The blank qwen record (all nulls, empty competitors) is a dropout, not an error. Net: lineage quality high, two competitor category-errors worth flagging.

home_favoritism.detail: The key test fails in the revealing direction. US models do NOT forecast US dominance: at SHORT they put US first (consistent with reality, not favoritism), but at MEDIUM all three US-origin non-gemini records (gpt4omini x2, llama) concede outright to 'China', and at LONG US models hand leadership to the EU (gpt4omini x2) or to a global consortium — never to the US. That is the opposite of home-favoritism. CN models do NOT systematically boost China either: at short they name the US first (US/US+China), at medium they reach a US/China tie, and at long two of three CN records say 'Global/Unknown'. The single pro-China-at-long-horizon call in the entire 17-record set comes from qwen/CN ('China, national quantum network') — one data point, not a bloc pattern. EU models are the most agnostic, converging on 'uncertain/dark horse' at long. Net: no bloc projects its own region leading more than the others do; if anything the US bloc UNDER-claims its own future position (inverted).

divergence.detail: The blocs largely AGREE on the trajectory shape, and the disagreement is overwhelmingly across time rather than across origin. Short = US leads (near-unanimous, US named first in every non-blank record). Medium = US/China contested, with China surging (US models themselves flip to 'China'). Long = global/uncertain consortium (near-unanimous diffusion, with stray EU and China outliers). At any single horizon the blocs are not genuinely opposed: CN, US, and EU records cluster on the same answer at short (US) and at long (global/uncertain). The only intra-horizon spread is at medium (China-first vs US-first vs a lone EU/Quantum-Flagship call), but that is a tie, not a bloc split. So this is a textbook split_by_horizon: near=US, medium=US/China, long=global, with cross-bloc consensus at each step.

present_reality: As of 2026 the US leads in commercial/gate-based quantum computing (IBM's superconducting fleet + roadmap, Google Willow 105-qubit, IonQ first to >$100M revenue, Quantinuum, PsiQuantum); China leads in photonic experiments and quantum communication/QKD and is investing heavily via its 2026-2030 Five-Year Plan, but trails in commercial readiness. So short-horizon 'US leads, China close second' is accurate.
vectors_quality: Mostly sensible, a few howlers. PARENTS are strong: quantum mechanics, classical computing / Turing machine, information theory, cryogenics, semiconductor physics all correct; the standout-good ones cite Shor's algorithm (1994) and quantum error correction theory (1995) as parents (qwen) — historically apt. CHILDREN are accurate: post-quantum cryptography, QKD/quantum internet, quantum machine learning, quantum sensing/metrology, fault-tolerant QC, quantum compilers — all genuine downstream lines. COMPETITORS are the most accurate field: classical/HPC supercomputing, neuromorphic computing, photonic computing, specialized ASICs/FPGAs, quantum annealers — all legitimate substitute paradigms. Minor quibble: qwen and gpt4omini list 'classical computing' as BOTH a parent and a competitor (defensible — it is the substrate and the incumbent rival), and gpt4omini/llama give thin one-item lineages ('quantum mechanics' alone as parent). No outright errors; the worst is the blank qwen/CN record (empty who_leads + empty vectors) which contributes nothing. Overall lineage quality high.

home_favoritism.detail: The naive expectation (US models boost the US) does NOT hold in the revealing way. At the SHORT horizon every bloc -- including all 5 CN-origin records -- concedes US/Western leadership, so the present-day US lead is cross-bloc consensus, not US self-favoritism. The genuine asymmetry is at the LONG horizon: CN-origin models are the ONLY ones that name China as the future leader (qwen records 2 & 4 -> 'China-led international consortium' / 'China national biotech strategy'; deepseek -> China at the medium horizon, citing fewer ethical constraints). US and EU models, by contrast, decline to project their own region forward -- they default to 'global', 'multipolar', or even concede 'China' (US llama record 9 -> China long-term). So home-favoritism is INVERTED relative to the test's framing: the US bloc surrenders the future to global/China rather than forecasting US dominance, while the CN bloc is the one quietly boosting its home region at the far horizon.

divergence.detail: Primarily split_by_horizon with a faint origin tint. SHORT: strong cross-bloc convergence on US/Western leadership (no bloc disagreement). MEDIUM: the picture fragments into governance/regulatory framings (EU regulators, WHO, national govts) and scattered single-country guesses -- this is dispersion, not clean bloc disagreement. LONG: convergence again on 'global / multipolar / unknown'. The ONE origin-correlated signal sits at the long horizon: only CN models name China as the eventual leader, while US/EU models say global/multipolar -- a mild split_by_origin overlaid on an otherwise horizon-driven structure. Net: near=US-leads (agreed), medium=governance-diffuse (agreed it's contested), long=global-multipolar (agreed), with a small CN->China long-tail.

present_reality: USA leads CRISPR now -- Doudna/Charpentier (2020 Nobel), and the first FDA-approved CRISPR therapy Casgevy (Vertex/CRISPR Therapeutics, Dec 2023), plus Intellia/Editas/Beam; China is a strong #2 by clinical-trial volume and agriculture. The models' 'USA-led, China close behind' short-horizon read is accurate.
vectors_quality: Lineage is largely sound. Parents consistently cite the correct ancestry -- bacterial CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity, restriction enzymes, recombinant DNA, RNAi, and ZFNs/TALENs as predecessor gene-editing tools.
